title: 2022 年全国硕士研究生招生考试 英语（二）

sections.title: Section I　完形填空
sections.dir: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 20 题 × 0.5 分。主线：写作是一份普通工作，拼的是优先次序与舍得。3、8、16 三处靠搭配定音。

paras.en: Harlan Coben believes that if you’re a writer, you’ll find the time; and that if you can’t find the time, then writing isn’t a priority and you’re not a writer. For him, writing is 1 job—a job like any other. He has 2 it with plumbing, pointing out that a plumber doesn’t wake up and say that he can’t work with pipes today.
paras.zh: 哈兰·科本认为，如果你是作家，你就会找到时间；如果你找不到时间，那就说明写作不是你的优先事项，你也不是作家。在他看来，写作就是一份普通的工作——一份和别的工作没什么两样的工作。他曾把写作与管道工的工作相比，指出管道工不会一觉醒来就说他今天没法跟水管打交道。

paras.en: 3 , like most writers these days, you’re holding down a job to pay the bills, it’s not 4 to find the time to write. But it’s not impossible. It requires determination and single-mindedness. 5 that most bestselling authors began writing when they were doing other things to earn a living. And today, even writers who are fairly 6 often have to do other work to 7 their writing income.
paras.zh: 如果你像如今大多数作家那样，靠一份工作来付账单，那么要找到写作的时间并不容易。但这并非不可能。它需要决心和心无旁骛。要记住，大多数畅销书作家开始写作时都在做别的事情谋生。而今天，即便是相当知名的作家，也常常得做其他工作来补贴写作收入。

paras.en: As Harlan Coben has suggested, it’s a 8 of priorities. To make writing a priority, you’ll have to 9 some of your day-to-day activities and some things you really enjoy. Depending on your 10 and your lifestyle, that might mean spending less time watching television or listening to music, though some people can write 11 they listen to music. You might have to 12 the amount of exercise or sport you do. You’ll have to make social media an 13 activity rather than a daily, time-consuming 14 . There’ll probably have to be less socializing with your friends and less time with your family. It’s a 15 learning curve, and it won’t always make you popular.
paras.zh: 正如哈兰·科本所暗示的，这是一个优先次序的问题。要让写作成为优先事项，你就得牺牲一些日常活动，以及一些你真正喜欢的事情。这取决于你的兴趣和生活方式：那可能意味着少花些时间看电视或听音乐，尽管有些人可以一边听音乐一边写作。你可能得减少锻炼或运动的时间。你得让社交媒体成为一种偶尔为之的活动，而不是每天耗时的一项习惯。与朋友社交的时间大概得减少，陪家人的时间也要减少。这是一条艰难的学习曲线，而且它并不总会让你讨人喜欢。

paras.en: There’s just one thing you should try to keep at least some time for, 16 your writing—and that’s reading. Any writer needs to read as much and as widely as they can; it’s the one 17 supporter—something you can’t do without.
paras.zh: 只有一件事，你应当尽量为它留出一点时间，那就是在你的写作之外再加上阅读。任何作家都需要尽可能多、尽可能广泛地阅读；阅读是那个不可或缺的支撑——是你不能没有的东西。

paras.en: Time is finite, the older you get, the 18 it seems to go. We need to use it as carefully and as 19 as we can. That means prioritizing our activities so that we spend most time on the things we really want to do. If you are a writer, that means— 20 —writing.
paras.zh: 时间是有限的，你年纪越大，它似乎就过得越快。我们需要尽可能谨慎、尽可能高效地利用它。这意味着要把我们的活动排出优先次序，把大部分时间花在我们真正想做的事情上。如果你是一名作家，那就意味着——最重要的是——写作。

items.exp: 定位首段 For him, writing is ___ job—a job like any other。破折号后的 a job like any other 就是对空的解释：“和别的活儿没两样”，即“普通的”，故 normal。difficult 与后文管道工那段平常口吻相反；steady（稳定的）说的是收入稳定，pleasant 说的是感受，本句都无对应线索。

定位 He has ___ it with plumbing, pointing out that a plumber doesn’t wake up and say...。with plumbing 加上 pointing out 引出的类比，说明是“拿写作和管道工作相比”，compare A with B 正合。confront 表“使面对、对质”，不能与 with 构成“相比”义；combine（结合）、confuse（混淆）与类比的逻辑不符。（参考册标 D，但 confronted 在此无法搭配，按原文语义取 B。）

定位空在句首、逗号后紧跟 like most writers these days, you’re holding down a job to pay the bills，主句是 it’s not easy to find the time。整句需要一个条件状语：“如果你像如今大多数作家那样靠工作付账单”，故 If。Once 表“一旦”，与“大多数作家”这种一般情形不合；Unless 反转逻辑；Through 是介词，不能引导从句。

定位 it’s not ___ to find the time to write. But it’s not impossible.。后句用 impossible 回应前句，构成“不容易，但并非不可能”的让步，故 easy。enough 会改变句子主语关系（It’s not enough to find the time 意为“找到时间还不够”），与 But it’s not impossible 接不上；wrong、strange 与“难易”这条线无关。

定位空在句首，后接 that 从句 most bestselling authors began writing when they were doing other things to earn a living。这是作者提请读者记住的事实论据，故 Remember that。Accept、Suppose 都要读者“接受一个假设”，而畅销作家当年边打工边写作是既成事实；Explain 作祈使句后不接 that 从句。

定位 even writers who are fairly ___ often have to do other work to supplement their writing income。even 表递进：连“相当有名”的作家也得兼职，才显出这一困境的普遍。well-advised（明智的）、well-informed（消息灵通的）、well-chosen（精选的）都不能修饰作家的名气，也与“收入不够”无呼应。

定位 even writers who are fairly well-known often have to do other work to ___ their writing income。前文说作家要 holding down a job to pay the bills，说明写作收入不够花，兼职只能“补贴”，故 supplement。generate 虽可与 income 搭配，却违背“收入不足”这一前提；donate（捐赠）、calculate（计算）与“另打一份工”无关。

定位 As Harlan Coben has suggested, it’s a ___ of priorities。a question of 是固定搭配，意为“……的问题”，下文 To make writing a priority 正承此展开，故 question。cause（原因）、purpose（目的）与 of priorities 搭配不通；condition 表“条件”，会把“优先次序”说成前提，逻辑颠倒。（参考册标 D，按搭配与语义取 C。）

定位 you’ll have to ___ some of your day-to-day activities and some things you really enjoy。紧接着列举的少看电视、少听音乐、少运动、少社交，全是“舍弃”，故 sacrifice。highlight（突出）、continue（继续）、explore（探索）都与“减掉”方向相反，其中 continue 最易误选，因为它与 activities 搭配最顺，却和全段“做减法”的主线相悖。

定位 Depending on your ___ and your lifestyle, that might mean spending less time watching television or listening to music。空与 lifestyle 并列，说明因人而异；后文 though some people can write while they listen to music 正是“兴趣不同”的例子，故 interests。relations（人际关系）、memories（记忆）、skills（技能）都解释不了“听不听音乐”的分歧。
定位 though some people can write ___ they listen to music。though 引出与前句“少听音乐”相反的例外，while 表“在……的同时”，强调两事并行，故 C。until、before 会把句子变成时间先后（“写到听音乐为止”“听音乐之前写”），because 会变成因果，都与“边听边写”不符。

定位 You might have to ___ the amount of exercise or sport you do。前有 spending less time，后有 less socializing、less time with your family，全段一个方向：减量，故 cut down on。put up with（忍受）、hang on to（紧抓不放）、make up for（弥补）都与“减少”相反。

定位 make social media an ___ activity rather than a daily, time-consuming 14。rather than 后的 daily 是反义提示，空必须与“每天”相对，故 occasional（偶尔的）。intelligent、intensive、emotional 都无法与 daily 构成对立，其中 intensive（密集的）方向最接近“耗时”，恰是 daily 的同侧而非反侧。
定位 rather than a daily, time-consuming ___。daily 与 time-consuming 修饰的只能是“习惯”——每天都要做、又耗时间的事，且与前句 an occasional activity 对举，故 habit。test、decision、plan 都不能被 daily 修饰成“每天耗时的事”，也不具备“偶尔—每天”这一对照。
定位 It’s a ___ learning curve, and it won’t always make you popular。前文是一连串“舍弃”，and 后又承认“不会总讨人喜欢”，可见这条曲线“艰难”，故 tough。gentle（平缓的）与“牺牲很多”相反；rapid 说的是速度，funny 说的是感受，本句都没有对应依据。
定位 keep at least some time for, ___ your writing—and that’s reading。破折号后点明“那就是阅读”，说明阅读是“除写作之外”还得留时间的事，故 in addition to。in place of（代替）会把阅读说成写作的替代品；in charge of（负责）、in response to（回应）与“另外还有”这层递加关系无关。

定位 it’s the one ___ supporter—something you can’t do without。破折号后的 can’t do without 就是“不可或缺”的同义解释，故 indispensable。innovative（创新的）、invisible（看不见的）、instant（即时的）都无法与“不能没有”对应，其中 invisible 与 indispensable 形近，最易看错。
定位 the older you get, the ___ it seems to go。the more... the more... 结构里前半是“年纪越大”，与“时间过得越快”这一常识搭配，且全段在讲 Time is finite，故 quicker。duller、quieter 与“时间流逝”的速度无关；harder 若指“更难熬”，则与后文“要抓紧用”的紧迫感不合。

定位 We need to use it as carefully and as ___ as we can。空与 carefully 并列修饰“使用时间”，后文 spend most time on the things we really want to do 指向“有效率地”，故 productively。peacefully、generously、gratefully 都是态度类副词，说明不了“时间用得有没有成效”。
定位 If you are a writer, that means—___—writing。破折号插入语起强调作用，全文结论是“写作最要紧”，故 above all。at most（至多）会把结论说成上限，in turn（依次）强调顺序，on average（平均）是统计口径，三者都无法承担总结强调的功能。

sections.title: Text 1　气候友好型鸡蛋
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主题：美国蛋业押注“气候友好型鸡蛋”。23 题问举例的作用，别选成“行业受挫”。

paras.en: On a recent sunny day, 13,000 chickens roam over Larry Brown’s 40 windswept acres in Shiner, Texas. Some rest in the shade of a parked car. Others drink water with the cows. This all seems random, but it’s by design, part of what the $6.1 billion U.S. egg industry bets will be its next big thing: climate-friendly eggs.
paras.zh: 不久前一个晴朗的日子，一万三千只鸡在得克萨斯州夏纳市拉里·布朗那片 40 英亩、常年刮风的土地上四处走动。有的躲在停着的汽车阴影里歇息，有的和牛一起饮水。这一切看似随意，实则出自精心设计——它是规模 61 亿美元的美国蛋业押注的下一个爆款：气候友好型鸡蛋。

paras.en: These eggs, which are making their debut now on shelves for as much as $8 a dozen, are still labeled organic and animal-friendly, but they’re also from birds that live on farms using regenerative agriculture—special techniques to cultivate rich soils that can trap greenhouse gases. Such eggs could be marketed as helping to fight climate change.
paras.zh: 这些鸡蛋如今刚上架，售价高达每打 8 美元，仍贴着有机、善待动物的标签，但它们还来自采用“再生农业”的农场——那是一套培育能固存温室气体的肥沃土壤的专门技术。这类鸡蛋可以“有助于应对气候变化”为卖点来推销。

paras.en: “I’m excited about our progress,” says Brown, who harvests eggs for Denver-based NestFresh Eggs and is adding more cover crops that draw worms and crickets for the chickens to eat. The birds’ waste then fertilizes fields. Such improvements “allow our hens to forage for higher-quality natural feed that will be good for the land, the hens, and the eggs that we supply to our customers.”
paras.zh: “我为我们的进展感到兴奋，”布朗说。他为总部在丹佛的 NestFresh Eggs 供蛋，眼下正增种覆盖作物，好引来蠕虫和蟋蟀供鸡啄食，鸡的粪便随后又给田地施肥。这些改进“让我们的母鸡能觅食到更优质的天然饲料，这对土地、对母鸡、也对我们供应给顾客的鸡蛋都有好处”。

paras.en: The egg industry’s push is the first major test of whether animal products from regenerative farms can become the next premium offering. In barely more than a decade, organic eggs went from being dismissed as a niche product in natural foods stores to being sold at Walmart. More recently there were similar doubts about probiotics and plant-based meats, but both have exploded into major supermarket categories. If the sustainable-egg rollout is successful, it could open the floodgates for regenerative beef, broccoli, and beyond.
paras.zh: 蛋业的这一推动，是对“再生农场的畜产品能否成为下一个高端品类”的第一次重大检验。在短短十几年间，有机鸡蛋从被斥为天然食品店里的小众产品，到摆上沃尔玛的货架。更近一些时候，益生菌和植物肉也曾遭遇类似质疑，但两者都迅速膨胀为超市里的大品类。如果可持续鸡蛋的推广成功，就可能为再生牛肉、西兰花以及更多品类打开闸门。

paras.en: Regenerative products could be a hard sell, because the concept is tough to define quickly, says Julie Stanton, associate professor of agricultural economics at Pennsylvania State University Brandywine. Such farming also brings minimal, if any, improvement to the food products (though some producers say their eggs have more protein).
paras.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州立大学布兰迪万分校农业经济学副教授朱莉·斯坦顿说，再生农产品可能不好卖，因为这个概念很难三言两语说清楚。这种耕作方式对食品本身的改善即便有也微乎其微（尽管有些生产者称自家鸡蛋蛋白质更多）。

paras.en: The industry is betting that the same consumers paying more for premium attributes such as free-range, non-GMO, and pasture-raised eggs will embrace sustainability. Surveys show that younger generations are more concerned about climate change, and some of the success of plant-based meat can be chalked up to shoppers wanting to signal their desire to protect the environment. Young adults “really care about the planet,” says John Brunnquell, president of Egg Innovations. “They are absolutely altering the food chain beyond what I think even they understand what they’re doing.”
paras.zh: 蛋业赌的是：那些愿意为散养、非转基因、牧场放养等高端属性多花钱的消费者，也会接受“可持续”。调查显示，年轻一代更关心气候变化；植物肉之所以成功，部分要归功于购物者想表达自己保护环境的意愿。Egg Innovations 总裁约翰·布伦奎尔说，年轻人“真的很在乎这个星球”，“他们正在实实在在地改变食物链，其程度甚至超出他们自己的理解”。

items.stem: The climate-friendly eggs are produced
opts: at the demand of regular shoppers
as a replacement for organic eggs
items.exp: 定位第二段 they’re also from birds that live on farms using regenerative agriculture—special techniques to cultivate rich soils：鸡蛋来自采用再生农业的农场，即“经过专门设计的农场”，故 D。A 与同段“每打高达 8 美元”相反；B 把“愿意多付钱的高端消费者”换成“普通购物者的要求”；C 与 still labeled organic 矛盾——它是叠在有机之上的新卖点，不是替代品。

items.stem: Larry Brown is excited about his progress in
items.exp: 定位第三段布朗的话：增种覆盖作物引来虫子供鸡吃，鸡粪肥田，母鸡因此觅食到优质饲料，而这一切“对土地、母鸡和鸡蛋都有好处”，构成一个可循环的体系，故 C。A 把“吸引蠕虫”读成“减少虫害”，方向相反；B 只抓“粪便肥田”一环，且 accelerated 无据；D 是结果，不是他“感到兴奋的进展”本身。

items.stem: The example of organic eggs is used in the paragraph 4 to suggest
opts: the doubts to over natural feeds
the setbacks in the eggs industry
the promotional success of super markets
items.exp: 定位第四段：有机鸡蛋十余年间从小众到沃尔玛，益生菌和植物肉也曾被质疑却“exploded into major supermarket categories”，末句 If the sustainable-egg rollout is successful, it could open the floodgates for regenerative beef, broccoli, and beyond 才是举例目的——说明再生农产品“有潜力”，故 C。B 把曾经的质疑当成主旨，方向反了；A 的 natural feeds 出自第三段，D 把“成为大品类”偷换成“超市促销成功”。

items.stem: It can be learned from the last paragraph that young people
opts: are reluctant to change their diet
are likely to buy climate-friendly eggs
items.exp: 定位末段：年轻一代更关心气候变化，购物者想借消费表达环保意愿，年轻人“真的很在乎这个星球”，并且“正在改变食物链”。把这层态度接到第二段的“气候友好型鸡蛋”上，可推知他们“很可能购买”，故 B。A reluctant 与 really care 相反；C 泛化成“对新食物好奇”，丢掉了环保这一动因；D 的 amazed at agricultural advances 文中无据。

items.stem: John Brunnquell would disagree with Julie Stanton over regenerative products’
items.exp: 定位第五段斯坦顿的判断 Regenerative products could be a hard sell, because the concept is tough to define quickly——对销路持保留；末段布伦奎尔则说年轻人 really care about the planet、are absolutely altering the food chain，明显看好。分歧落在“市场前景”，故 A。B 是斯坦顿单方面的说法，布伦奎尔并未就“定义”表态；D 的道德意涵文中无人提及。（此题存疑：真题排版 A、C 两项文字几乎重复，疑为重出，答案册标 A。）

sections.title: Text 2　退而不休的美国人
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主题：越来越多美国人退休后继续工作。27 题问“美国人的看法”，不是作者观点。

paras.en: More Americans are opting to work well into retirement, a growing trend that threatens to upend the old workforce model.
paras.zh: 越来越多的美国人选择一直工作到退休之后，这一日益明显的趋势有可能颠覆旧的劳动力模式。

paras.en: One in three Americans who are at least 40 have or plan to have a job in retirement to prepare for a longer life, according to a survey conducted by Harris Poll for TD Ameritrade. Even more surprising is that more than half of unretirees—those who plan to work in retirement or went back to work after retiring—said they would be employed in their later years even if they had enough money to settle down, the survey showed.
paras.zh: 哈里斯民意调查为 TD Ameritrade 所做的一项调查显示，40 岁及以上的美国人中，每三人就有一人已经或计划在退休后继续工作，为更长寿的人生做准备。更令人意外的是，调查显示，超过半数的“退而不休者”——即计划退休后继续工作或退休后又重返职场的人——表示即使钱已足够安顿下来，他们晚年仍会继续工作。

paras.en: Financial needs aren’t the only culprit for the “unretirement” trend. Other reasons, according to the study, include personal fulfillment such as staying mentally fit, preventing boredom or avoiding depression. About 72% of “unretirees” respondents said that they would return to work once retired to keep mentally fit while 59% said it would be tied to making ends meet.
paras.zh: 经济需要并不是“退而不休”趋势的唯一原因。研究称，其他原因还包括个人成就感，比如保持头脑敏锐、防止无聊或避免抑郁。约 72% 的“退而不休”受访者表示，退休后会重返工作岗位以保持头脑敏锐；59% 的人则表示这与维持生计有关。

paras.en: “The concept of retirement is evolving,” said Christine Russell, senior manager of retirement at TD Ameritrade. “It’s not just about finances. The value of work is also driving folks to continue working past retirement.”
paras.zh: “退休这个概念正在演变，”TD Ameritrade 退休业务高级经理克里斯汀·拉塞尔说，“这不只是钱的问题。工作的价值也在促使人们过了退休年龄仍继续工作。”

paras.en: One reason for the change in retirement patterns: Americans are living longer. The share of the population 65 and older was 16% in 2018, up 3.2% from the prior year, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. That’s also up 30.2% since 2010. Older Americans are also the fastest-growing segment of the U.S. workforce, and boomers are expected to live longer than previous generations. The percentage of retirement-age people in the labor force has doubled over the past three decades. About 20% of people 65 and older were in the workforce in February, up from an all-time low of 10% in January 1985, according to money manager United Income.
paras.zh: 退休模式改变的一个原因是：美国人活得更久了。美国人口普查局的数据显示，2018 年 65 岁及以上人口占比为 16%，比上一年上升 3.2%，与 2010 年相比也上升了 30.2%。老年人还是美国劳动力中增长最快的群体，而“婴儿潮”一代预计将比前几代人更长寿。过去三十年里，处于劳动年龄以上的人口的劳动参与率翻了一番。资产管理公司 United Income 的数据显示，今年 2 月约 20% 的 65 岁及以上人口仍在工作，而 1985 年 1 月曾低至 10% 的历史最低点。

paras.en: Because of longer life spans, Americans are also boosting their savings to preserve their nest eggs, the TD Ameritrade study showed, which surveyed 2,000 adults between 40 to 79. Six in 10 “unretirees” are increasing their savings in anticipation of a longer life, according to the survey. Among the most popular ways they are doing this, the company said, is by reducing their overall expenses, securing life insurance or maximizing their contributions to retirement accounts. Seniors are living longer, but planning for the extended years is key.
paras.zh: TD Ameritrade 的这项研究调查了 2000 名 40 至 79 岁的成年人。研究显示，由于寿命延长，美国人也在增加储蓄以保住自己的养老钱。调查称，每十个“退而不休者”中有六个正在为更长的人生增加储蓄。该公司表示，他们最常用的做法包括削减总体开支、购买人寿保险，或尽可能多地向退休账户缴款。老年人活得更久，但为多出来的这些年做规划才是关键。

paras.en: Unfortunately, many people who are opting to work in retirement are preparing to do so because they are worried about making ends meet in their later years, said Brent Weiss, a co-founder at Baltimore-based financial-planning firm Facet Wealth. He suggested that preretiree should speak with a financial adviser to set long-term financial goals.
paras.zh: 巴尔的摩理财规划公司 Facet Wealth 的联合创始人布伦特·韦斯说，遗憾的是，许多选择退休后继续工作的人之所以做准备，是因为担心晚年入不敷出。他建议临近退休的人应与理财顾问沟通，设定长期财务目标。

paras.en: “The most challenging moments in life are getting married, starting a family and ultimately retiring,” Weiss said. “It’s not just a financial decision, but an emotional one. Many people believe they can’t retire.”
paras.zh: “人生中最具挑战性的时刻是结婚、组建家庭，以及最终的退休，”韦斯说，“这不仅是财务决定，也是情感决定。很多人认为自己退不了休。”

items.stem: The survey conducted by Harris Poll indicates that
opts: over half of the retirees are physically fit for work
the old workforce is as active as the younger one
one in three Americans enjoy earlier retirement
more Americans are willing to work in retirement
items.exp: 定位第二段：One in three Americans who are at least 40 have or plan to have a job in retirement；更惊人的是超过半数“退而不休者”说即使钱够也不收手。调查指向“越来越多美国人愿意退休后继续工作”，故 D。A 把 more than half of unretirees 偷换成“半数以上退休者身体适合工作”；C 与“打算退休后工作”正相反；B 的“老年劳动力与年轻人一样活跃”在文中没有这样的比较。

items.stem: It can be inferred from Paragraph 3 that Americans tend to think that
opts: retirement may cause problems for them
boredom can be relieved after retirement
the mental health of retirees is overlooked
items.exp: 定位第三段：除经济原因外，还有 personal fulfillment such as staying mentally fit, preventing boredom or avoiding depression——正因为退休会带来无聊、抑郁这些“问题”，人们才要靠工作去防，故 A。B 把“为防无聊而工作”倒读成“退休后无聊自然缓解”；C 的 overlooked 无据，文中这是受访者自己给出的理由；D 谈经济贡献，与本段的“个人实现”不在一条线上。

items.stem: Retirement patterns are changing partly due to
items.exp: 定位第五段首句 One reason for the change in retirement patterns: Americans are living longer，随后用 65 岁以上人口占比、劳动参与率翻倍来印证，故 C。A 劳动力短缺、B 人口增长都不是文中给出的原因，属常识性联想；D 生活成本上升虽与“经济需要”沾边，但题干问“模式改变的原因”，原文明确写出的第一条是寿命延长。

items.stem: Many retirees are increasing their savings by
items.exp: 定位第六段：Among the most popular ways they are doing this... is by reducing their overall expenses, securing life insurance or maximizing their contributions to retirement accounts——“削减总开支”即 spending less，故 D。A 的 stocks 全文未提，是最典型的“合理但无据”；B、C 说的是“继续工作挣钱”，与“增加储蓄的手段”不是同一件事。

items.stem: With regard to retirement, Brent Weiss thinks that many people are
items.exp: 定位第七段：Weiss 说很多人是“因为担心晚年入不敷出”才准备退休后继续工作，并建议 preretiree 应找理财顾问设定长期目标；末段又说“很多人认为自己退不了休”。可见他认为人们“没准备好”，故 A。B unafraid 与 worried 相反；C 的 disappointed 文中没有依据；D enthusiastic 来自他对退休“情感化”的描述，不等于“准备充分”。

sections.title: Text 3　“暗黑模式”与消费者选择
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主题：“暗黑模式”如何操纵界面，又该由谁约束。31 题考头两段的定义句，别被 hidden costs 带跑。

paras.en: We have all encountered them, in both our personal and professional lives. Think about the times you felt tricked or frustrated by a membership or subscription that had a seamless sign-up process but was later difficult to cancel. Something that should be simple and transparent can be complicated, intentionally or unintentionally, in ways that impair consumer choice. These are examples of dark patterns.
paras.zh: 无论是在私人生活还是职业生活中，我们都遇到过它们。想一想那些让你觉得上当或恼火的时刻：某项会员或订阅服务注册时顺畅无碍，之后却难以取消。本应简单透明的事情，却可能有意无意地变得复杂，从而损害消费者的选择。这些就是“暗黑模式”的例子。

paras.en: First coined in 2010 by user experience expert Harry Brignull, “dark patterns” is a catch-all term for practices that manipulate user interfaces to influence the decision-making ability of users. Brignull identifies 12 types of common dark patterns, ranging from misdirection and hidden costs to “roach motel” where a user experience seems easy and intuitive at the start, but turns difficult when the user tries to get out.
paras.zh: “暗黑模式”一词由用户体验专家哈里·布里格纳尔于 2010 年首次提出，是对一类做法的统称：这类做法操纵用户界面，以影响用户的决策能力。布里格纳尔归纳出 12 种常见的暗黑模式，从误导、隐藏费用，到“蟑螂旅馆”——开始时体验似乎轻松直观，用户想抽身离开时却变得困难。

paras.en: In a 2019 study of 53,000 product pages and 11,000 websites, researchers found that about one in 10 employs these design practices. Though widely prevalent, the concept of dark patterns is still not well understood. Business and nonprofit leaders should be aware of dark patterns and try to avoid the gray areas they engender.
paras.zh: 在 2019 年一项涵盖 5.3 万个商品页面和 1.1 万个网站的研究中，研究者发现约每十个就有一个使用了这类设计手法。尽管相当普遍，暗黑模式这一概念却仍未得到充分理解。企业和非营利组织的领导者应当了解暗黑模式，并尽量避免由此产生的灰色地带。

paras.en: Where is the line between ethical, persuasive design and dark patterns? Businesses should engage in conversations with IT, compliance, risk, and legal teams to review their privacy, and include in the discussion the customer/ user experience designers and coders responsible for the company’s user interface, as well as the marketers and advertisers responsible for sign-ups, checkout baskets pricing, and promotions. Any or all these teams can play a role in creating or avoiding “digital deception.”
paras.zh: 合乎道德的说服性设计与暗黑模式之间的界线在哪里？企业应当与信息技术、合规、风险和法律团队沟通，审查自身的隐私问题，并把负责公司用户界面的客户/用户体验设计师和程序员，以及负责注册、购物车定价和促销的营销与广告人员，一并纳入讨论。这些团队中的任何一个或全部，都可能在制造或避免“数字欺骗”中起作用。

paras.en: Lawmakers and regulators are slowly starting to address the ambiguity around dark patterns, most recently at the state level. In March, the California Attorney General announced the approval of additional regulations under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) that “ensure that consumers will not be confused or misled when seeking to exercise their data privacy rights.” The regulations aim to ban dark patterns — this means prohibiting companies from using “confusing language or unnecessary steps such as forcing them to click through multiple screens or listen to reasons why they shouldn’t opt out.”
paras.zh: 立法者和监管者正慢慢开始处理暗黑模式带来的模糊地带，最近的动作发生在州一级。今年 3 月，加州总检察长宣布批准《加州消费者隐私法》（CCPA）下的附加条例，以“确保消费者在行使数据隐私权时不会被弄糊涂或误导”。这些条例旨在禁止暗黑模式——即禁止企业使用“令人困惑的措辞或不必要的步骤，例如迫使用户点过多个页面，或听人解释他们为何不该选择退出”。

paras.en: As more states consider promulgating additional regulations, there is a need for greater accountability from within the business community. Dark patterns also can be addressed on a self-regulatory basis, but only if organizations hold themselves accountable, not just to legal requirements but also to industry best practices and standards.
paras.zh: 随着更多州考虑颁布附加条例，企业界内部也需要更强的问责。暗黑模式也可以在自我监管的基础上加以解决，但前提是各机构对自己负责——不仅对法律要求负责，也对行业最佳做法与标准负责。

items.stem: It can be learned from the first two paragraphs that dark patterns
items.exp: 定位第二段定义句 practices that manipulate user interfaces to influence the decision-making ability of users，第一段又说 impair consumer choice——即“损害用户的决策能力”，故 C。A improve 与 manipulate、impair 相反；B 的“泄露信息牟利”文中未提，属凭常识补足；D 说“提醒用户注意隐藏费用”，而 hidden costs 本身就是暗黑模式的一种手法，方向正好颠倒。

items.stem: The 2019 study on dark patterns is mentioned to show
items.exp: 定位第三段：5.3 万个商品页、1.1 万个网站中约 one in 10 使用这类设计，紧接一句 Though widely prevalent 是作者对研究结果的概括——举这个研究是为说明暗黑模式“普遍存在”，故 D。A、C 都转向“危害有多大”，本段强调的是“数量之多、分布之广”；B 的 complex designs 说的是设计繁复，与“普及程度”不是一回事。

items.stem: To handle digital deception, businesses should
items.exp: 定位第四段 Businesses should engage in conversations with IT, compliance, risk, and legal teams to review their privacy，并让设计师、程序员、营销人员一同参与讨论——即“与相关团队沟通”，故 B。A 的顾客反馈、C 的独立机构、D 的职业培训文中均无，是三个“听起来合理”的替换项，其中 A 最容易凭常识误选。

items.stem: The additional regulations under the CCPA are intended to
items.exp: 定位第五段：附加条例要 ensure that consumers will not be confused or misled when seeking to exercise their data privacy rights，即“保护消费者不被误导、不被骗”，故 B。A 与条例禁止 forcing them to click through multiple screens 恰好相反——它要拆掉这些步骤，而不是“引导用户走完”；C 把“消费者权利”说成“公司权利”；D 的 problematic content 与本段讲的“退出流程”无关。

items.stem: According to the last paragraph, a key to coping with dark patterns is
items.exp: 定位末段：there is a need for greater accountability from within the business community；Dark patterns also can be addressed on a self-regulatory basis, but only if organizations hold themselves accountable——关键在“企业自律”，故 B。A 的新法律要求是“此外”还有的事，不是关键；C 严格监管属外部约束，正被 but only if 转向内部自律；D 的消费者安全意识全文未提。

sections.title: Text 4　一堂伦理课的效果
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主题：一堂伦理课真能改变行为。39 题 Strohminger 只是“存疑”，不是否定，别选 permanent。

paras.en: Although ethics classes are common around the world, scientists are unsure if their lessons can actually change behavior; evidence either way is weak, relying on contrived laboratory tests or sometimes unreliable self-reports. But a new study published in Cognition found that, in at least one real-world situation, a single ethics lesson may have had lasting effects.
paras.zh: 尽管伦理课在世界各地都很常见，科学家却不清楚这些课程是否真能改变行为；正反两方面的证据都很薄弱，靠的是人为设计的实验室测试，或有时并不可靠的自我报告。但发表在《认知》杂志上的一项新研究发现，至少在一个真实情境中，一堂伦理课可能产生了持久的影响。

paras.en: The researchers investigated one class session’s impact on eating meat. They chose this particular behavior for three reasons, according to study co-author Eric Schwitzgebel, a philosopher at the University of California, Riverside: students’ attitudes on the topic are variable and unstable, behavior is easily measurable, and ethics literature largely agrees that eating less meat is good because it reduces environmental harm and animal suffering.
paras.zh: 研究者考察了一节课对吃肉行为的影响。据论文合著者、加州大学河滨分校哲学家埃里克·施维茨格贝尔介绍，他们选择这一行为有三点理由：学生对此事的态度多变且不稳定，行为易于测量，而伦理学界大体上一致认为少吃肉是好的，因为这样可以减少对环境的破坏和动物的痛苦。

paras.en: Half of the students in four large philosophy classes read an article on the ethics of factory-farmed meat, optionally watched an 11-minute video on the topic and joined a 50-minute discussion. The other half focused on charitable giving instead. Then, unknown to the students, the researchers studied their anonymized meal-card purchases for that semester-nearly 14,000 receipts for almost 500 students.
paras.zh: 四个大班哲学课中，一半学生阅读了一篇关于工厂化养殖肉类伦理的文章，自愿观看了一段 11 分钟的相关视频，并参加了一场 50 分钟的讨论。另一半学生则改为关注慈善捐赠。随后，在学生们不知情的情况下，研究者分析了他们那个学期匿名的餐卡消费记录——近 500 名学生的约 1.4 万张收据。

paras.en: Schwitzgebel predicted the intervention would have no effect; he had previously found that ethics professors do not differ from other professors on a range of behaviors, including voting rates, blood donation and returning library books. But among student subjects who discussed meat ethics, meal purchases containing meat decreased from 52 to 45 percent -and this effect held steady for the study’s duration of several weeks. Purchases from the other group remained at 52 percent.
paras.zh: 施维茨格贝尔原本预测这一干预不会有效果；他此前发现，伦理教授在一系列行为上与其他教授并无差别，包括投票率、献血和归还图书馆书籍。但在讨论过肉类伦理的学生受试者中，含肉的餐食消费从 52% 降到 45%——而且这一效应在为期数周的研究期间保持稳定。另一组的消费则维持在 52%。

paras.en: “That’s actually a pretty large effect for a pretty small intervention,” Schwitzgebel says. Psychologist Nina Strohminger at the University of Pennsylvania, who was not involved in the study, says she wants the effect to be real but cannot rule out some unknown confounding variable. And if real, she notes, it might be reversible by another nudge: “Easy come, easy go.”
paras.zh: “对这么小的干预来说，这其实是个相当大的效应，”施维茨格贝尔说。未参与该研究的宾夕法尼亚大学心理学家妮娜·施特罗明格说，她希望这个效应是真的，但无法排除某些未知的混淆变量。她还指出，即便效应为真，也可能被另一次“轻推”逆转：“来得容易，去得也容易。”

paras.en: Schwitzgebel suspects the greatest impact came from social influence—classmates or teaching assistants leading the discussions may have shared their own vegetarianism, showing it as achievable or more common. Second, the video may have had an emotional impact. Least rousing, he thinks, was rational argument, although his co-authors say reason might play a bigger role. Now the researchers are probing the specific effects of teaching style, teaching assistants’ eating habits and students’ video exposure. Meanwhile, Schwitzgebel-who had predicted no effect-will be eating his words.
paras.zh: 施维茨格贝尔推测，最大的影响来自社会影响——主持讨论的同学或助教可能分享了自己的素食习惯，让人觉得素食既可做到也更常见。其次是视频可能带来的情感冲击。他认为最不奏效的是理性论证，尽管他的合著者认为理性可能作用更大。目前研究者正在细查教学风格、助教饮食习惯和学生接触视频情况的具体影响。而曾断言“不会有效”的施维茨格贝尔，只好收回自己的话。

items.stem: Scientists generally believe that the effects of ethics classes are
items.exp: 定位首段 scientists are unsure if their lessons can actually change behavior; evidence either way is weak——“说不清有没有用、两方面证据都弱”，即“难以判断”，故 A。B narrowly interpreted、D poorly summarized 谈的是“解读/总结得好不好”，与“证据不足、结论未定”不是一回事；C difficult to ignore 与 unsure 意思相反。

items.stem: Which of the following is a reason for the researchers to study meat eating?
opts: It is a behavior easy to measure.
It is important to students’ health
It is a hot topic in ethics classes.
items.exp: 定位第二段列出的三条理由：attitudes are variable and unstable, behavior is easily measurable, and ethics literature largely agrees that eating less meat is good——第二条正是“行为易于测量”，故 B。A 的“在学生中普遍”文中未说；C 谈健康，原文给的理由是减少环境破坏与动物痛苦；D 的 hot topic 与“态度多变不稳定”不是同一条理由。

items.stem: Eric Schwitzgebel’s previous findings suggest that ethics professors
opts: are seldom critical of their students
are less sociable than other professors
are not sensitive to political issues
items.exp: 定位第四段：他此前发现 ethics professors do not differ from other professors on a range of behaviors, including voting rates, blood donation and returning library books——在献血、还书这些带道德色彩的行为上并不比别人好，故 D。A、B、C 是把“没有差别”硬掰成“不批评学生/不善社交/对政治不敏感”，其中 C 借 voting rates 设套，但投票率不等于政治敏感度。

items.stem: Nina Strohminger thinks that the effect of the intervention is
items.exp: 定位第五段：Strohminger 说 she wants the effect to be real but cannot rule out some unknown confounding variable，又说若为真也可能被另一个“轻推”逆转，Easy come, easy go——态度是“不确定”，故 C。A permanent 与 reversible 相反，是最强干扰；B predictable 与“无法排除混淆变量”矛盾；D unrepeatable 她并未质疑可重复性。

items.stem: Eric Schwitzgebel suspects that the students’ change in behavior
opts: is a result of multiple factors
items.exp: 定位末段：他推测最大影响来自 social influence（同学、助教的示范），其次视频的情感冲击，最弱的是理性论证，且团队正分别探查教学风格、助教饮食习惯、视频接触——行为改变是多个因素叠加的结果，故 C。A 的“心理益处”、B 的“可作统计分析”、D 的“自我发展的标志”都不是他的推测内容，其中 B 借文中的百分比数据设套。

sections.title: Section II Part B　选小标题
sections.dir: Read the following text and answer the questions by choosing the most suitable subtitles from the list A-G for each numbered paragraph (41-45). There are two extra subtitles which you do not need to use. Make your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 五段各有一个动作核心：循序渐进、听身体信号、养成习惯、空手比划、结伴锻炼。D、G 是多余项。
sections.intro:
How to get active again?

Getting back into exercise can be a challenge in the best of times, but with gyms and in-person exercise classes off-limits to many people these days, it can be tricky to know where to start. And it’s important to get the right dose of activity. “Too much too soon either results in injury or burnout,” says Mary Yoke, PhD, a faculty member in the kinesiology department at Indiana University in Bloomington. The following simple strategies will help you return to exercise safely after a break.

blocks.en: Don’t try to go back to what you were doing before your break. If you were walking 3 miles a day, playing 18 holes of golf three times a week, or lifting 10-pound dumbbells for three sets of 10 reps, reduce activity to ½ mile every other day, or nine holes of golf once a week with short walks on other days, or use 5-pound dumbbells for one set of 10 reps. Increase time, distance, and intensity gradually. “This isn’t something you can do overnight,” say Keri L. Denay, MD, lead author of a recent American College of Sports Medicine advisory that encourages Americans to not overlook the benefits of activity during the pandemic. But you’ll reap benefits such as less anxiety and improved sleep right away.
blocks.zh: 不要试图回到中断之前的状态。如果你原本每天走 3 英里、每周打三次 18 洞高尔夫，或用 10 磅哑铃做三组、每组 10 次，就把活动量降到隔天走半英里，或每周打一次 9 洞、其余日子短距离散步，或改用 5 磅哑铃做一组 10 次。然后逐步增加时间、距离和强度。“这不是一晚上就能做到的事，”凯里·L. 德奈医生说。她是美国运动医学会一份近期建议书的第一作者，该建议书提醒美国人不要忽视疫情期间运动的好处。但好处马上就能尝到，比如焦虑减轻、睡眠改善。
blocks.exp: 本段动作线很清楚：把每天 3 英里减到隔天半英里、18 洞减到 9 洞、10 磅哑铃减到 5 磅，然后 Increase time, distance, and intensity gradually，末句 This isn’t something you can do overnight 更点明“急不得”——起点低、慢慢加，故 C。A 讲“坚持成习惯”是 43 段的事；E 讲“听身体信号”对应 42 段，两段都以“别过量”擦边，是本段最强的干扰。

blocks.en: If you’re breathing too hard to talk in complete sentences, back off. If you feel good, go a little longer or faster. Feeling wiped out after a session? Go easier next time. And stay alert to serious symptoms, such as chest pain or pressure, severe shortness of breath or dizziness, or faintness, and seek medical attention immediately.
blocks.zh: 如果你喘得说不出完整的句子，就退一步。如果感觉良好，就多练一会儿或加快一点。一次训练后感觉精疲力竭？下次就轻一些。同时要警惕严重症状，如胸痛或胸部压迫感、严重气短或头晕，或要昏倒的感觉，一旦出现应立即就医。
blocks.exp: 本段通篇是身体反馈：喘得说不出整句话就 back off，感觉好就加量，累垮了下次就轻一点，还要警惕 chest pain、shortness of breath、dizziness 等 serious symptoms——落点是“按身体信号调整”，故 E。D Talk with your doctor 只在最后 seek medical attention 处擦边，但那是“出现严重症状时”的例外处理，全段主体是自我感知，不是就医。

blocks.en: Consistency is the key to getting stronger and building endurance and stamina. Ten minutes of activity per day is a good start, says Marcus Jackovitz, DPT, a physical therapist at the University of Miami Hospital. All the experts we spoke with highly recommend walking because it’s the easiest, most accessible form of exercise. Although it can be a workout on its own, if your goal is to get back to Zumba classes, tennis, cycling, or any other activity, walking is also a great first step.
blocks.zh: 坚持是变得更强、建立耐力和体力的关键。迈阿密大学医院的物理治疗师、物理治疗博士马库斯·雅科维茨说，每天活动十分钟是个不错的开始。我们采访过的所有专家都极力推荐走路，因为这是最简便、最容易做到的锻炼形式。走路本身就可以算一次锻炼；而如果你的目标是重回尊巴课、网球、骑行或别的项目，走路也是很好的第一步。
blocks.exp: 本段首句就是结论句 Consistency is the key to getting stronger and building endurance and stamina，接着给出“每天十分钟起步”“走路最易坚持”，落点在“天天做、别断”，故 A。C 的“低起点慢加量”虽也与“十分钟起步”沾边，但本段的重心词是 consistency 与 per day，且 41 段才是讲减量与渐进。

blocks.en: Even if you can’t yet do a favorite activity, you can practice the moves. With or without a club or racket, swing like you’re hitting the ball. Paddle like you’re in a kayak or canoe. Mimic your favorite swimming strokes. The action will remind you of the joy the activity brought you and prime your muscles for when you can get out there again.
blocks.zh: 即使你暂时还做不了喜欢的运动，也可以练习动作。有没有球杆或球拍都行，照着击球的动作挥一挥。像在皮划艇或独木舟里那样划桨。模仿你最喜欢的泳姿。这些动作会唤起这项运动曾带给你的快乐，也能让你的肌肉为重新上场做好准备。
blocks.exp: 本段反复落在“做动作”上：practice the moves、swing like you’re hitting the ball、Paddle like you’re in a kayak、Mimic your favorite swimming strokes——不必真上场，先照着比划，故 F Go through the motions。G Round out your routine 讲的是让锻炼项目更全面，本段没有“补足短板、搭配项目”的意思，只是“空手练动作”，是最像的干扰。

blocks.en: Exercising with others “can keep you accountable and make it more fun, so you’re more likely to do it again,” Jackovitz says. You can do activities such as golf and tennis or take a walk with others and still be socially distant. But when you can’t connect in person, consider using technology. Chat on the phone with a friend while you walk around your neighborhood. FaceTime with a relative as you strength train or stretch at home. You can also join a livestream or on-demand exercise class.
blocks.zh: 雅科维茨说，和别人一起锻炼“能让你更有责任感，也更有趣，因此你更可能坚持下去”。你可以和朋友一起打高尔夫、打网球或散步，同时保持社交距离。但如果无法当面相聚，不妨借助技术：散步时和朋友通电话，在家做力量训练或拉伸时和亲戚视频。你也可以参加直播课或点播课。
blocks.exp: 本段首句 Exercising with others “can keep you accountable and make it more fun”，后面给的全是结伴办法：一起打球散步、边散步边打电话、和家人视频、上直播课——核心动作是“不要一个人练”，故 B Don’t go it alone。G 的“丰富锻炼内容”与本段的“与他人一起”不是一回事，若只抓到最后“参加课程”这一句，容易误选 G。

sections.title: Section III　翻译
sections.dir: Translate the following text from English into Chinese. Write your translation on ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.note: 按句给分：切句→定主谓→调语序。thinking outside the box 与 with which 定语从句最难。

paras.en: Although we try our best, sometimes our paintings rarely turn out as originally planned. Changes in the light, the limitations of your painting materials and the lack of experience and technique mean that what you start out trying to achieve may not come to life the way that you expected.
paras.zh: 尽管我们尽了最大努力，有时我们的画作却很少能如最初设想的那样呈现。光线的变化、绘画材料的局限，以及经验和技法的欠缺，都意味着你起初想要达到的效果，未必能以你期待的方式呈现出来。

paras.en: Although this can be frustrating and disappointing, it turns out that this can actually be good for you. Unexpected results have two benefits: you pretty quickly learn to deal with disappointment and realize that when one door closes, another opens. You also quickly learn to adapt and come up with creative solutions to the problems the painting presents and thinking outside the box will become your Second nature. In fact, creative problem-solving skills are incredibly useful in daily life, with which you’re more likely to be able to find a solution when problem arises.
paras.zh: 尽管这可能令人沮丧、令人失望，但事实证明，这其实对你大有好处。意想不到的结果有两点好处：你会很快学会面对失望，并认识到一扇门关上时，另一扇门会打开。你也会很快学会变通，为画作带来的问题想出有创意的解决办法，而跳出常规思考将成为你的第二天性。事实上，创造性地解决问题的能力在日常生活中极其有用；有了它，问题出现时你更有可能找到解决办法。

words: 令人沮丧的、令人气馁的
跳出固有思维、打破常规

sections.title: Section IV Part A　应用文（邀请信）
sections.dir: Suppose you are planning a campus food festival for the international students. Please 1) tell them about the festival and 2) invite them to participate. You should write about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET. Do not use your own name. Use “Li Ming” instead. (10 points)
sections.note: 两个任务点都要落地：①活动的时间、地点、内容 ②邀请并说明怎么报名。署名固定 Li Ming。
sections.sample:
Dear international students,

I am writing to invite you to our campus food festival, which will be held on the playground from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Saturday, May 21.

The festival is organized for students from different countries. Each of you is welcome to set up a stall and offer a dish typical of your hometown, and at noon there will be a short introduction to each cuisine. Tableware and basic cooking facilities will be provided; you only need to bring the ingredients.

To take part, please send your name and the dish you plan to cook to the Student Union office before May 15. I look forward to tasting your food.

Yours sincerely,
Li Ming
tips: 第一段一句话交代“写信目的 + 活动时间地点”，不要一上来就写意义，信息要具体到日、时、地点
第二段写清活动内容与对收信人的要求（设摊位、带食材、介绍家乡菜），这是题目 1) 的落点
第三段给出参与方式与截止时间，回应题目 2) invite them to participate，否则不算完成邀请
对国际学生用词宜浅显，避免长难句；署名固定 Li Ming，不编造真实姓名与地址

sections.title: Section IV Part B　图表作文
sections.dir: Write an essay based on the following chart. In your writing, you should 1) interpret the chart, and 2) give your comments. You should write about 150 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.sample:
The bar chart shows changes in China’s express delivery volume from 2018 to 2020, with rural areas highlighted separately. In 2018 the national total stood at 51 billion parcels, and by 2020 it had climbed to 83 billion, a rise of more than 60 percent. Deliveries in rural areas grew even faster, from 12 billion to 30 billion, so their share of the total rose from roughly a quarter to over a third.

Two forces explain the trend. The first is online shopping: as e-commerce platforms reach almost every county, buying goods on a phone has become routine. The second is better rural logistics: delivery stations have been built in villages, and roads and cold-chain facilities have improved, which allows farmers to send out produce as well as receive parcels.

The figures are encouraging. A robust express network narrows the gap between city and countryside and gives rural residents both cheaper goods and new income. Investment in rural logistics should therefore continue.
tips: 第一段只做“读数”：总体 51→83、农村 12→30，再补一句“农村占比由约四分之一升到三分之一以上”，比逐条报数更有力
第二段归因要分两层：需求端（网购普及）+ 供给端（农村网点、道路与冷链），两条都要落到“快递量”上
数值单位是“10 亿件”，写 51、83 时务必点明单位，不能误当百分数
结尾给一句方向性判断（缩小城乡差距、继续投农村物流），不要再开新话题
